root_idea.summary: The root centers on confusion, hesitation, and lack of guidance.
root_idea.development: The evidence presents a movement from not knowing where to turn and repeatedly wandering to mental or spiritual perplexity; related descriptions extend the lack of guidance to land without way-signs.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form عَمِهَ rather than the QAC imperfect lemma يَعْمَهُ.

senses.definition: To be confused or perplexed and wander without knowing or following the right course.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage, the imperfect active form commonly occurs with فِي and a domain of transgression or error. It describes mental or spiritual loss of direction and wandering, not physical blindness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of land, to be destitute of signs or landmarks of the way.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical expression applied to land that gives no guidance to safety.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wrong someone without sure information.
Confused or perplexed, unable to see the right course, and going repeatedly to and fro in error.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description; it may also describe failure to know the right argument, plea, or allegation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression ذَهَبَتْ إِبِلُهُ العُمَّهَى: his camels went away and no one knew where they had gone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed idiomatic expression concerning camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having no signs of the way to guide to safety.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine adjective is applied to land.
